data.title: eXoZymes Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results and Provides Business Update at 5PM ET Today
data.description:
LOS ANGELES, CA / ACCESS Newswire / November 19, 2026 / Today, eXoZymes Inc. (NASDAQ:EXOZ) ("eXoZymes") - a pioneer of AI-enhanced enzymes that transform abundant feedstock into valuable nutraceuticals and novel medicines - will host an investor webinar at 5:00 PM Eastern Time to discuss results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provide an update on recent business developments.

Michael Heltzen, CEO of eXoZymes, states, "We're entering an exciting new phase for eXoZymes as we advance our lead product toward commercial manufacturing while expanding our pipeline of high-value molecules. Our progress with Curia and the advancement of additional product candidates demonstrate how we intend to turn our technology into a repeatable engine for commercial opportunities. We believe our ability to move rapidly from discovery toward scalable production is what sets our platform apart."

Third quarter highlights

  • Commercial manufacturing preparations underway with Curia: In September, eXoZymes selected Curia as its commercial-scale manufacturing partner for NCT, the rare natural molecule behind its lead supplement brand, Tyferyn. Technology transfer began in the fourth quarter of 2026, with the collaboration intended to support larger-scale manufacturing in 2027, representing an important step toward commercial readiness.
  • Tyferyn introduced as the brand for human use: eXoZymes introduced Tyferyn as the new brand name for its lead nutraceutical ingredient focused on human wellness applications. The rebranding establishes a distinctive, consumer-friendly identity as the Company advances preparations for commercialization.
  • Product pipeline expands: eXoZymes has advanced two additional supplement candidates through proof of concept, demonstrating the broader potential of its cell-free biomanufacturing platform. Product SAPPHIRE, targeting joint comfort, has begun scale-up activities, while Product AMETHYST, targeting mental stress, focus and energy, has also completed proof of concept. The programs support the Company's strategy of building a diversified portfolio of high-value products using its shared enzyme technology and development capabilities.
  • Operational and financial update: Operating expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were $3.05 million, compared with $2.52 million for the same period in 2025. Net loss was $2.24 million for the quarter and $7.49 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. Net loss for the quarter includes a $0.77 million non-cash gain from the change in fair value of warrant liabilities. The Company ended the quarter with $3.26 million in cash and cash equivalents, which the Company expects will support operations through the beginning of 2027.

Investors and interested parties can access the live webinar through eXoZymes' investor relations website at:
https://video.exozymes.com/exoz-investor-update-3q26-nov-19

Michael Heltzen, CEO of eXoZymes, will lead the call and be joined by select members of the management team to review recent developments and ongoing initiatives. A recording and transcript of the conference call will also be made publicly available following the event.

About eXoZymes
Founded in 2019, eXoZymes is pioneering a cell-free biomanufacturing platform that uses AI-enhanced enzymes - called exozymes - to make valuable natural products and new analogs outside living cells. The company's platform is designed to replace inefficient extraction and petrochemical processes with a scalable way to produce high-value molecules for nutraceutical and pharmaceutical markets.

eXoZymes is building a portfolio of biosolutions across NCT - now Tyferyn for human use - cannabinoid analogs, santalene, and other high-value natural product molecules, with potential commercialization paths that include partnerships, licensing and joint ventures. Learn more at exozymes.com

data.title: Why Micron, Broadcom and other AI stocks gave up their gains Thursday
data.description:
By Hannah Pedone

The Anthropic IPO enthusiasm faded while China concerns intensified

Micron's stock closed down about 2% on Thursday.

For a period of time on Thursday, it looked like the excitement over Anthropic's initial public offering would give artificial-intelligence stocks a much-awaited boost. But the trading action turned decidedly more mixed.

Shares of companies like Nvidia (NVDA), Micron Technology (MU) and Broadcom (AVGO) that initially saw a broad-based AI rally on Thursday morning closed lower. Some of the AI stocks that closed in positive territory on Thursday, including Intel (INTC) and Coherent (COHR), had their own specific catalysts.

Part of the issue may be that Anthropic's IPO prompted investors to shift around their holdings, according to Iskandar Rakhmatov, a portfolio manager at quantitative-strategy research platform Zeus Quanto.

"Investors who wanted the purest AI exposure got it today, and some of them sold Nvidia and other chip names to fund the new position," he told MarketWatch.

Granted, the excitement around Anthropic itself has also waned. Shares (ANT) opened 34% higher midday Thursday, but they pared those gains to close up 17% from their IPO price of $83.

Jack Amy, a quantitative-trading analyst at European digital wealth platform Moneyfarm, noted that at first, the Anthropic IPO "gave broader U.S. equities a lift, helping to steady nerves after a choppy week for tech."

"However, those wider gains have since pared back as macro concerns, specifically around tightening financial conditions and what that means for the capital-intensive AI trade, continue to weigh on sentiment," he added in emailed comments.

There are also renewed jitters about export policies after a report from a short seller discussed whether Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) chips have made it into Chinese servers.

"The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships. AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations," an AMD spokesperson told MarketWatch.

"The China issues are likely to permeate across the semi industry as export controls are tightened," said Michael Casper, senior market strategist at wealth-management firm HB Wealth.

Investors have generally been worried that the U.S. government would take a tougher tack on sales of advanced technology to China in light of recent turmoil involving Nvidia.

See also: Jensen Huang was a 'China salesman' for Nvidia. His exit is weighing on Chinese tech stocks.

Heading into Thursday's trading day, D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria told MarketWatch that Anthropic's IPO was "pivotal" for the AI investment cycle.

Luria said that a successful IPO could "extend the cycle by years," while an unsuccessful one could "stall investment" into the ecosystem.

See also: Can Anthropic's IPO do for the stock market what Nvidia's earnings couldn't?

Morningstar analyst Martin Szumski doubted the IPO would "fully turn around what has been very bearish sentiment lately." One reason is that investors saw Anthropic's prospectus weeks ago and knew "relatively what to expect."

The AI stocks that managed to hold onto some gains on Thursday had some idiosyncratic drivers. Shares of Coherent closed up 1% after the optical company announced a new buyback program, while shares of Intel closed up 2% following reports of remarks from a conference indicating that the company locked in an outside customer for its 18A manufacturing technology.

CoreWeave's stock, meanwhile, gave up a double-digit percentage gain and closed down 6%, despite a co-founder's disclosure that he purchased $30 million of the company's bruised bonds with the intention to hold them until maturity in 2031.

Don't miss: A CoreWeave co-founder just made an unconventional $30 million wager on its battered bonds

-Hannah Pedone

data.title: Rising healthcare costs push Medicare Part B premiums higher
data.description:
By Jessica Hall

The premiums will increase by $6.50, to $209.40 a month

Higher Medicare Part B premiums will erode part of the Social Security cost-of-living adjustment for 2027.

Medicare Part B premiums, which cover doctor's appointments, outpatient hospital services, and certain home health services, will rise about 3.2% to $209.40 a month in 2027 amid a projected increase in healthcare spending, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services said on Tuesday.

The premium will rise by $6.50 a month from $202.90 in 2026, which marked the first time premiums topped $200 a month. The higher premium for 2027, which would total $2,512.80 a year, was roughly in line with expectations set by the Social Security and Medicare Board of Trustees in June.

The annual deductible for all Medicare Part B beneficiaries will be $292 in 2027, an increase of $9 from the annual deductible of $283 in 2026, CMS said.

"The increase in the 2027 Part B standard premium and deductible is mainly due to projected increases in healthcare spending," CMS said in a statement.

The Trump administration recently sent $90 checks to 20.8 million middle-class older adults, characterizing the payment as a way to help offset the expected Medicare premium increase.

The Medicare Part B premium is automatically deducted from Social Security checks, eroding part of the recently announced cost-of-living adjustment. The COLA will be 3.6% in 2027, up from 2.8% this year. For the average beneficiary, the COLA will add about $75 to their monthly check.

If your income exceeds specific tiered limits - such as over $112,000 for individual tax returns or $240,00 for married couples for 2027 - you pay an additional monthly surcharge known as the income-related monthly adjustment amount, or IRMAA. This surcharge is added to the standard monthly premiums for Medicare. The 2027 IRMAA surcharges range from $83.70 to $502.40 for an individual depending on income, CMS said.

The news of the new Medicare Part B premium comes during the Medicare open-enrollment period that runs through Dec. 7. Eligible adults can switch from traditional Medicare to a private Medicare Advantage plan, change from one Medicare Advantage plan to another, and join or change a Medicare Part D prescription-drug plan. These changes take effect on Jan. 1.

-Jessica Hall

data.title: 'I felt so seen': Why families across America are laughing - and crying - over SNL's 'Sister' sketch
data.description:
By Beth Pinsker

The late-night comedy sketch does the impossible by making female caregivers feel seen

A screenshot from Saturday Night Live's "Sister" comedy sketch.

With all that's been going on in the world in the past week - the Nvidia (NVDA) scandal, the FAA flight stoppage, the Microsoft outage, the midterm election fallout - it's incredible that "Saturday Night Live" had the bandwidth to strike a cultural chord with a sketch about the all-too-real sibling imbalance in caregiving.

More than 2.2 million had watched the official YouTube clip of the late-night comedy institution's "Sister" sketch, featuring host John Mulaney, by noon on Monday, and other links were circulating the web.

"Sister" hit my feed first thing Sunday morning, just as I was about to go on stage at a conference to talk about - you guessed it - caregiving. The merciless impact on women who care for family members is a big part of my talk, which stems from my own experiences of caregiving and the book I wrote about it, called "My Mother's Money."

It's more than just the emotional toll, but also the out-of-pocket costs - which AARP now pegs at an average of $11,500 per year - long-term career costs, dented retirement savings and lower Social Security benefits. Mulaney jokes that if you text "dad fell," your sister will quit her job, break her lease and fly across the country to step into the breach. So true.

I felt seen. Everyone in my orbit felt seen.

"So sad, and so true," said Nancy Brenner, a writer and content strategist in New York who has been caring for her mother for years.

Kim Elliott, who founded a newsletter for caregivers called "Gray Monster" - which has the tag line that they're there to help "because we know your brother won't" - heard from more than 100 of her subscribers over the weekend. She thought the skit resonated so much because it was so true. "The punchline is that 'Sister' is free. And she is, to everyone but herself," said Elliot.

"That's the 'daughter tax,'" said Lily Vittayarukskul, founder of WaterLily, a company that helps families connect with long-term-care policies. "When families don't plan for the cost of care, they can end up paying for it with a daughter's financial future."

Feeling seen is a big deal. Caregiving is invisible labor, and the people who do it also feel invisible. I saw this repeatedly over the weekend when talking to various clusters of people at the Bogleheads conference, which focuses on financial education for do-it-yourself investors who follow the model set by Vanguard founder Jack Bogle. People just wanted to talk. They had fear in their eyes. Many were deep in a care situation for an aging parent, and also were seeing the train coming straight for them. Some were worried about their children.

There were plenty of men in these conversations, all just as concerned and involved as the women I met. Caregiving is a lot for anyone. But there is statistical truth in the view that it hits women harder than men; between 60% and 70% of family caregivers these days are women, depending on which survey you pick. And this represents a lot of progress: It used to be closer to 100% women, but go back more than 30 or 40 years and it was just expected, not measured.

"I laughed at 'Sister,' and then I winced, because I've met that brother more than once," said David Goodman, co-founder of CompassCare, which coordinates care for families when neither brother or sister can be there 24/7. "Look at how far parenting has come. A generation ago, paternity leave barely existed and nobody expected a dad at the pediatrician's office. Today, both are normal. Caregiving for aging parents is on the same path, just a few decades behind. Right now, it falls disproportionately on women. It can and should be shared, and that shift is already under way."

But we're not quite there yet. At one point over the weekend, I found myself talking to a table full of men about caregiving. One asked me if I had siblings who helped me on my caregiving journey.

I looked around and said, "Oh, I don't think my usual joke about this is going to land with this group." He said try it. I said, "I have an older brother."

At a table full of women, we'd all have a good laugh about this, because we know that it means just what the SNL skit lays out in dark humor: You get a call and drop everything, while your proverbial brother goes on with his life. But the men at the table just blinked.

I asked the original questioner if he had siblings. He said he had two sisters; they were closer to their parents, and that's why they ended up doing more. Of course, I nodded. He then asked the right follow-up question: "What could I do better to help?"

I said that the No. 1 complaint I hear from female caregivers about their siblings, no matter the gender, is that they second-guess and criticize, but never step in to do the work. It's incredibly frustrating to be buried under the weight of caregiving and then have somebody from the outside telling you that you are doing it wrong. (See also: Jennifer Grey's Home Instead commercial reprising her "Ferris Bueller" character.) So the best thing a sibling on the sidelines can do is call to ask how the caregiver is doing, and offer love and support instead of potshots.

Maybe that's the big takeaway that the SNL "Sister" moment will have. With the clip being passed from sibling to sibling - one poster on social media said she group-texted the clip to her sisters and excluded her brother, but added that others might want their brothers to see it - it will spark some "aha!" moments and some loving conversations.

I can already imagine the one happening in the Seidell family, after SNL writer Streeter Seidell posted that he dedicated the piece, which he co-wrote with Mikey Day and Simon Rich (with an assist from Chase Rosenberg), to his sister Heidi.

"Family caregivers rarely see their lives reflected in pop culture. Caregiving is an incredibly serious subject, but sometimes levity is the best entry point into a difficult conversation. I'm grateful to SNL for opening that door," said Gray Monster's Elliot.

Or, perhaps, you can dream bigger. Ai-jen Poo, who has dedicated her whole career to being an advocate for caregivers, posted this: "Here's the quiet part: it doesn't have to be this way...this dynamic is the result of avoidable policy choices...that we can change!"

data.title: Amtrak Expands Airo Fleet with Higher-Capacity Trains
data.description:
Amtrak Expands Airo Fleet with Higher-Capacity Trains

Eight 10-car trainsets to bring more seats to the Northeast Regional

Amtrak is expanding its Airo fleet with eight additional 10-car trainsets to help meet the growing demand for Northeast Regional service on the Northeast Corridor. The new trains, expected to begin entering service in 2031, will each seat more than 640 customers.

The higher-capacity trains will build on the Airo fleet that will begin serving the Northeast Regional in late 2027. With more seats per departure, these trains will allow additional customers to enjoy the same modern amenities and accessibility features.

“Demand for train travel isn’t slowing down, and neither are we,” said Amtrak Interim President Byl Herrmann. “For our customers, that means more seats, more availability when travel is busiest, and more chances to find a fare that fits their budget.”

“Building on the historic expansion Amtrak has seen under President Trump, these new trainsets will allow Amtrak to service thousands more annually, boosting profitability and supporting our hardworking rail workers and builders. In the last year alone, Amtrak has received over $2.5 billion for new trainsets across the country, as well as funding to revitalize flagship stations in America’s national and financial capitals--D.C. and New York,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy. “And we’re just getting started. The Golden Age of Rail is safer, more connective, and more affordable for American passengers.”

More Capacity, Same Airo Experience

In FY25, 15.2 million customers traveled on the Acela and Northeast Regional. These higher-capacity trainsets will expand seating in one of the nation’s busiest transportation corridors. With two additional cars, each train will offer about 34% more seats than the eight-car Airo trainsets planned for Northeast Regional service. The 10-car trains will offer the full Airo experience, with room for a growing number of Northeast Regional customers.

Northeast Regional Airo Testing Underway

Testing is underway on Northeast Regional Airo trains, with passenger service planned to begin in late 2027. Customers will see eight-car trains when service begins, with the higher-capacity 10-car trainsets following in 2031.

Part of a Broader Fleet Transformation

Amtrak is in the midst of a historic service overhaul and fleet expansion. In the last year, Secretary Duffy and USDOT invested $465.8 million in federal funding to overhaul the customer experience at Washington Union Station, put over $200 million towards the revitalization of New York's Penn Station, and awarded Amtrak $2.05 billion to acquire 43 Made-in-America trainsets to replace Amtrak’s aging fleet, among other milestones.

This is part of the Trump Administration's vision for the Golden Age of Rail. Recent and upcoming milestones include:

  • NextGen Acela: Introduced into passenger service on the Northeast Corridor in 2025, bringing a new travel experience to Amtrak’s premium high-speed service.
  • Amtrak Cascades: Airo entered passenger service in September 2026, marking the fleet’s first deployment in the country. Additional trainsets will continue entering service through mid-2027.
  • Northeast Regional: Airo trains are planned to begin carrying customers in late 2027, with Amtrak Virginia routes to follow.
  • Higher-Capacity Northeast Regional: Eight 10-car trainsets are planned to begin entering passenger service in 2031.

Built for America, by America

Airo trainsets are manufactured by Siemens Mobility at its facilities in Sacramento, California, and Lexington, North Carolina. More than 3,500 parts come from nearly 100 suppliers across 31 states, supporting manufacturing jobs well beyond the Northeast Corridor.

“These trainsets represent the work of skilled manufacturing, engineering, and supply chain teams across our U.S. operations. Together, they are helping deliver the next generation of passenger rail technology while supporting reliable service for travelers nationwide,” said Tobias Bauer, Managing Director, Siemens Mobility North America.

See where the Airo fleet is made.

REACTIONS:

“As someone who regularly travels between Connecticut and D.C. by train, I am thrilled that Amtrak is expanding their trains to accommodate more passengers,” said Senator Richard Blumenthal. “These new trains mean more options for the thousands of people who rely on Amtrak every day.”

“As a member of the Northeast Corridor, Delaware knows the critical role Amtrak and our railways play in our way of life — it’s how we strengthen our workforce, build community, and create an economy that works for all of us,” said Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester. “I’m excited to see the expansion of Amtrak’s Airo fleet to ensure we continue developing safe, reliable rail travel that meets the demand of travelers on the Northeast Corridor and across the nation.”

“New Jersey and our country badly need federal investment to modernize our nation’s rail and transit systems,” said Senator Cory Booker. “Amtrak’s addition of eight higher-capacity Airo trains are part of the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law’s investment in passenger rail. For Northeast Regional riders in New Jersey, including those boarding at Newark Penn Station or Trenton Transit Center, these trains will offer more seats and a more accessible ride. That’s good news for Jersey riders and for the American workers building these trains with parts from suppliers in 31 states.”

“Recently, I had the opportunity to see the new Airo fleet and meet the incredible Amtrak workers and technicians who help make them run in Bear, Delaware,” said Senator Chris Coons. “Amtrak is a vital part of our economy and I’m proud to have voted for the funding that made these new, modern trains possible. I will continue to work with my colleagues in Congress to keep investing in Amtrak and our rail infrastructure.”

“The Northeast Corridor is our region’s economic lifeblood, but aging equipment has held us back for too long,” said Senator Kirsten Gillibrand. “Expanding Amtrak’s new Airo fleet is exactly the kind of modern, high-capacity transportation upgrade I fought to deliver through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. These additional train cars will ease congestion, help ensure reliable service during peak hours, and finally give riders the 21st-century transit system they deserve.”

“Every year, millions of travelers and commuters rely on Amtrak to connect them to cities across the Northeast,” said Senator Chris Van Hollen. “We passed the infrastructure modernization law to upgrade dated transportation systems across America, and the expanded fleet of high-capacity Airo trains, supported by $22 billion through that bill, will provide safer, more comfortable, and more energy-efficient rail service for passengers in Maryland and across the East Coast.”

“I’m glad to see Amtrak connecting more people throughout the bustling Northeast Corridor,” said Senator Sheldon Whitehouse. “These new, larger trains will help reduce congestion on the roads and open up more seats for travelers and business passengers.”

“I’m proud to have voted for the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law that made this expansion of Amtrak’s next-generation fleet possible,” said Representative Brendan Boyle. “These new trains will deliver comfortable, reliable service for even more Philadelphians and grow our city’s economy by bringing new visitors to local businesses.”

“As a regular rail commuter, I understand how important it is for people to have accessible and reliable transportation,” said Representative Rosa DeLauro. “This announcement of eight additional trainsets on Amtrak will support that goal by adding more seats to a busy corridor. I am glad that Amtrak is expanding its fleet to accommodate more customers, and I will continue to support resources to expand and improve our transportation system.”

“Amtrak is investing to better serve millions of Northeast Regional travelers by increasing rider capacity along the Northeast Corridor. These service additions will mean faster commutes, greater accessibility, and more affordable Amtrak trips,” said Representative George Latimer. “As a regular Amtrak user, I look forward to seeing this expansion in action and riding the new cars on my next trip to Washington, D.C.!”

“I’m extremely proud of the hardworking North Carolinians who are the driving force behind Siemens in Lexington,” said Representative Addison McDowell. “These new Amtrak trains are another example of American manufacturing getting the job done right in our backyard, supporting good-paying jobs here in the Sixth District and strengthening our economy.”

“I am grateful that the new Amtrak Airo fleet will help get New Jerseyans where they need to go faster and more reliably. So many residents in my district rely on rail travel, and now they’ll have access to more seats, more affordable fares, and upgraded amenities and accessibility features that will make train travel more convenient and sustainable,” said Representative LaMonica McIver. “As someone who regularly uses the train, it’s great to witness the hard work and collaboration from all partners that goes into a project like this, and I am excited to see it come to life in NJ-10 and beyond.”

“Adding new, modern trains to Amtrak’s fleet means a smoother, more accessible ride for the thousands of New Jerseyans who rely on rail to get where they need to go,” said Representative Rob Menendez. “This investment is a major win for our region, and I’ll keep fighting in Congress to deliver the safe, reliable transportation our communities deserve.”

“The expansion of Amtrak’s Airo fleet will meaningfully improve the experience of rail commuters in the Northeast Corridor, including the thousands of Baltimoreans who take an Amtrak train to and from work every day,” said Representative Kweisi Mfume. “I have consistently supported funding for Amtrak, and I look forward to continuing that support on behalf of Maryland commuters as we enter the 120th Congress.”

“The Northeast Corridor is the backbone to a region that would be the world’s fifth-largest economy on its own. Since the pandemic, Amtrak has set new ridership records on the NEC each year and demand is continuing to grow,” said Representative Seth Moulton. “I’m pleased to see Amtrak meeting the moment by renewing its fleet with new NextGen Acela and Airo trainsets and also ordering additional 10-car Airo trainsets too. These upgrades will enable more frequent service and added flexibility to help passengers traveling up and down the NEC.”

“As demand for fast, efficient transportation grows, I am proud to support Amtrak’s Northeast Corridor fleet expansion,” said Representative Jerrold Nadler. “By adding new, modern passenger rail cars, Amtrak is taking a significant step toward meeting the increased capacity and quality needs. Congress must continue fighting to ensure robust funding for passenger rail, both on the Northeast Corridor and across the national network.”

“Amtrak’s Airo fleet expansion will improve rail service for millions of riders who rely on the Northeast Regional, including in the Philadelphia area,” said Representative Mary Gay Scanlon. “I was proud to support the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) which made the Airo fleet possible, and I applaud Amtrak for making investments that expand access to rail travel and significantly upgrade the rider experience.”

About Amtrak®

Amtrak is seizing a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to transform rail and Retrain Travel. By modernizing, enhancing, and expanding trains, stations, and infrastructure, Amtrak is meeting the rising demand for train travel. Amtrak offers unforgettable experiences to more than 500 destinations across 46 states and parts of Canada. data.title: ICE Review: Canola Swings Higher
data.description:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Partially recovering from Wednesday's pull back, Intercontinental Exchange canola futures reversed course on Thursday taking back a portion of the losses.

An analyst said he wasn't entirely sure as to what drove up canola Thursday, but noted it's "up one day, down the next" movement this week. The analyst suggested canola could see losses on Friday.

Although gains in crude oil turned softer on Thursday, there was still enough spillover to boost some of the vegetable oils, including canola. Additional support came from upticks in Chicago soyoil and European rapeseed.

Declines in Chicago soybeans and soymeal, plus those in Malaysian palm oil limited the upside in the Canadian oilseed.

The Canadian dollar was relatively steady on Thursday afternoon, with the loonie at 69.76 U.S. cents, compared to Wednesday's close of 69.80.

There were 63,520 canola contracts traded on Thursday, compared to 90,131 on Wednesday. Spreading accounted for 40,266 contracts traded.
